title: Weft project file (weft.json)
description: Shared resources and tool settings of a Weft project (SPEC §10). Every member is optional; an argument given to a tool overrides the file, and the file overrides the defaults.

$schema.description: This schema, for editors. Ignored by Weft.

tokens.description: DTCG token files, in layer order: a later file overrides an earlier one; or one DTCG resolver document (`*.resolver.json`) whose modifiers give contexts such as light and dark (SPEC §10.3).

package.description: An npm package in node_modules of the project directory or a parent; its package.json names the catalog file in "weft": { "catalog": … } (SPEC §10.2).

catalog.description: Catalogs merged over the core catalog: libraries, each owning the kinds under its prefix, and at most one project catalog without a prefix that adds the project's kinds, props and variants (SPEC §10.4). A library may come from an npm package.

actions.description: The host's action names; on-* values are checked against them.

data.description: A JSON Schema of the host data model; bindings are checked against it (SPEC §10.5).

fragments.description: Fragments the project's screens place with <use>: each name maps to a file of fragment markup (SPEC §10.7).

mode.description: "strict" reports unknown elements and attributes as errors, "lenient" as warnings (SPEC §8). Used by `weft validate` and as the default of weft_validate's strict argument.

write.description: Rewrite the file in place instead of printing it.

format.description: How `weft fmt` writes the canonical form. The form itself has no options (SPEC §3).

context.description: Also list each element's context entries (SPEC §2.3) after its readbacks.

explain.description: How `weft explain` reads a screen back.

data.description: Sample data file the bindings read, relative to the project file. Default: no data.

tokens.description: DTCG token files to render with, in layer order, or one DTCG resolver document; they replace the project's tokens. Default: the project's tokens.

outDir.description: Directory, relative to the project file, that output files go to. Default: next to the input file.

appearance.description: Which context of the resolver's light and dark modifier (SPEC §10.3) the page is rendered with, and the page's color-scheme. Default: the resolver's default context.

render.description: Static HTML pages from screens (`write-page`, the Claude Code plugin's render).

outDir.description: Directory, relative to the project file, that output files go to. Default: next to the input file.

source.description: Keep the canonical screen in a leading comment, so the importer gives it back exactly instead of reading the code by convention.

context.description: Whether the source comment carries the screen's context (SPEC §2.3): `keep` or `strip`. The CLI's `--context` overrides it.

data.description: Sample data (a JSON file, relative to the project file) the page shows: bindings read it and `<each>` repeats over it. Default: none, the page is a template for a host to fill.

html.description: Static HTML pages with CSS and no script (`weft html`).

outDir.description: Directory, relative to the project file, that output files go to. Default: next to the input file.

typescript.description: Write TSX with typed props instead of JSX.

namespace.description: The C# namespace of the generated page classes and of the `Weft` helper classes, such as `Acme.Screens`. The CLI's `--namespace` overrides it.

winui.description: WinUI 3 pages for the Windows App SDK (`weft winui`) and the shared `WeftTokens.xaml` (`weft winui-tokens`).

schema.description: The JSON Schema of the canonical documents the project's catalog admits, `document.schema.json` (`weft schema`). Default folder: standard output.

export.description: Code generated from screens, one section per target.

name.description: The name of the imported catalog. Default: the manifest's file name without its extension.

version.description: The version of the imported catalog.

prefix.description: The prefix of the imported catalog: it owns the kinds named `<prefix>-…` and requires the core, so it loads beside a project catalog (SPEC §10.4). Default: none, which makes it the project catalog.

cem.description: Catalogs from a Custom Elements Manifest (`weft import-cem`).

outDir.description: Directory, relative to the project file, that output files go to. Default: next to the input file.

context.description: Whether the context kept in a frame's plugin data enters the document (SPEC §2.3): `keep` or `drop`. `drop` suits files from outside the team.

figma.description: Frames of a Figma file, read through the REST API (the plugins' `figma-pull` script).

import.description: Screens imported from other formats, and catalogs from a Custom Elements Manifest, one section per source.

markupChars.description: UTF-16 code units of one markup argument.

dataChars.description: UTF-16 code units of the JSON of weft_render's data argument.

patchesChars.description: UTF-16 code units of the JSON of one patch list.

projectChars.description: UTF-16 code units of the JSON of a project argument.

diagnostics.description: Diagnostics listed in one result; the rest are counted.

inputElements.description: JSON values in one call's arguments.

limits.description: Bounds on what one tool call may ask of the server.

context.description: Whether weft_patch may change a screen's context (SPEC §2.3): "read-only" refuses every context patch (W512); weft_context still reads it.

mcp.description: The MCP server, when the host starts it with this project file. A project passed as a tool argument never changes these.

tokensDir.description: Folder, relative to the project file, that the plugin's design-md script writes mapped tokens to. Default: next to the design system.

plugins.description: Settings of plugins, one object per plugin name. The plugins listed here are checked; the content of any other is not.

fileName.description: Relative to the project file, separated by "/", inside the project directory.
